subject: principles-of-flight

concepts.teaching_target: Show the legacy syllabus term longitudinal dihedral as the tailplane set at a lower incidence than the mainplane, and connect that geometry to longitudinal/pitch stability about the lateral axis.

source.syllabus_notes: Exact POF wording defines longitudinal dihedral as tailplane lower incidence than mainplane and links it to stability in the pitching plane/about the lateral axis.
source.technical_reference: Longitudinal Stability about the Lateral Axis; Figures 1-22 to 1-24
source.technical_notes: CG/lift/tail-force geometry and restoring tailplane action support the pitch-stability teaching relationship.

concepts.teaching_target: For the conventional/plain trailing-edge flap case used by the questions, show flap extension moving the centre of pressure aft and creating a nose-down pitching moment.

source.document: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, Chapter 6
source.notes: FAA text explicitly states that the plain flap increases camber/lift/drag and moves the centre of pressure aft, producing a nose-down pitching moment.

concepts.teaching_target: In a left turn, show ball left/inside = slip, centred = coordinated, and ball right/outside = skid.

source.document: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, Chapter 8
source.notes: FAA figure/text explicitly distinguish slipping, coordinated and skidding turns and state that the ball moves inside in a slip and outside in a skid.

concepts.teaching_target: Define aeroelastic flutter as destructive self-excited oscillation and show a control-surface mass balance/counterweight ahead of the hinge reducing flutter susceptibility.

source.document: FAA AC 23.629-1B and FAA Airframe Handbook
source.notes: FAA guidance identifies control-surface mass balance as a flutter-prevention measure and describes adding weight forward of the hinge line for static balance.

concepts.teaching_target: Contrast horn balance and inset-hinge aerodynamic balance, showing how area ahead of the hinge lets aerodynamic force assist surface movement and reduce pilot control force.

source.document: FAA Airframe Handbook and UK CAA Standards Document 10
source.reference: Aerodynamic balance methods; horn balance and inset hinge
source.notes: Official guidance lists horn balance and inset-hinge methods and explains the aerodynamic assistance produced by control-surface area ahead of the hinge.
